{{Quote|It was undoubtedly a simple task of extricating the Foreman. We are the masters of technology. To think the Republic could devise machinery to slow us down is laughable.|A Techno Union employee|<ref name="shadowfeed" />}}
A '''mission''' to the remote [[Prison/Legends|prison]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Delrian/Legends|Delrian]] was undertaken by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]]. After his [[Battle of Metalorn (Clone Wars)|capture]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] on [[Metalorn/Legends|Metalorn]], Techno Union [[Foreman/Legends|Foreman]] [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]] was transported to Delrian by request of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. The prison's security firm, however, was owned by the Separatist-aligned [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], allowing the CIS and the Techno Union access to details of the prison's layout and security.

Tambor was allowed a visit by several of his staff&mdash;two [[Skakoan/Legends|Skakoan]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], posing as [[Skakoan legal deputies|legal deputies]], and a [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifting]] [[Clawdite/Legends|Clawdite]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] known as [[Nuri]]. Once inside the facility, the two Skakoans [[Death/Legends|blew themselves up]], killing Tambor's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] guards, while Nuri bypassed automated security with Techno Union technology and whisked Tambor to safety. The foreman traveled to [[Denus]], [[Foundry/Legends|Foundry]] to recuperate, while the Republic attempted to keep his escape hushed up.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|Anakin Skywalker's capture of Wat Tambor during the Metalorn mission had caught Darth Sidious by surprise. The move could have potentially destabilized the war&hellip;|[[Historian/Legends|Historian]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]], in a historical tome|<ref name="nec" />}}
After a failed [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Coruscant Insurrection|attack]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], ten [[Standard month/Legends|months]] into the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] dispatched [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] to the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] [[Factory world/Legends|mechworld]] of [[Metalorn/Legends|Metalorn]], where the Techno Union was producing [[C-B3 cortosis battle droid/Legends|C-B3 cortosis battle droids]]. The droids were the brainchild of Techno Union [[Foreman/Legends|Foreman]] and CIS [[Combat engineer (Techno Union)/Legends|Supervising Combat Engineer]] [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]], and had been used in the attack on Coruscant. Skywalker was able to shut down the facility and also managed to snare Tambor, exceeding expectations.<ref name="nec" />

Skywalker's capture of Tambor was a surprise to [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], the alter ego of Republic [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who was playing both sides and manipulating the war for his own end. Tambor's capture could potentially have destabilized the war and tipped the balance in favor of the Republic, which was not what Sidious wanted. In his capacity as Supreme Chancellor, Palpatine ordered that Tambor be relocated to [[Delrian/Legends|Delrian]], a remote [[Prison/Legends|prison]] world,<ref name="nec" /> where he would be kept under guard by a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of eight Republic [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], in addition to local security. The detainment center employed an external security firm, which happened to be owned by the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], an ally of the Confederacy and the Techno Union. Thus, the Separatists had access to intimate knowledge of the facility's defensive capabilities, security complement, and layout. Rather than launch a full-scale attack, the Techno Union planned a smaller rescue attempt,<ref name="shadowfeed" /> and [[Nuri]], a [[Clawdite/Legends|Clawdite]] [[Changeling/Legends|changeling]] from [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]], was hired to assist them.<ref name="nec" />

==The mission==
{{Quote|He is the Separatists' Techno Union Foreman, as well as a combat engineer. A brilliant strategist. And extremely dangerous&mdash;an expert at fighting machines, and a master of defense technologies. He is also an expert at escape.|[[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], on Wat Tambor|<ref name="ant">''[[Boba Fett: A New Threat]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Databank_Wat_Tambor_emir_of_Ryloth.png|thumb|left|300px|Wat Tambor, Skakoan foreman of the Techno Union]]
Tambor was permitted a visit by members of his staff. Two elite [[Skakoan/Legends|Skakoan]] [[Commando/Legends|commandos]], posing as [[Skakoan legal deputies|legal deputies]], visited the facility with a disguised Nuri. Nuri brought secret state-of-the-art Techno Union technology, which would allow him to bypass the prison's automated defenses.<ref name="shadowfeed" /> Once inside the center, the two legal deputies breached their [[Pressure suit/Legends|pressure suits]], releasing the compressed [[Methane/Legends|methane]] inside. This caused a large explosion,<ref name="nec" /> [[Death/Legends|killing]] Tambor's [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Trooper/Legends|trooper]] guard as well as the two Skakoans.<ref name="shadowfeed" />

In the ensuing chaos, Nuri was able to infiltrate Tambor's holding area and whisk the foreman to safety.<ref name="nec" /> Using the Techno Union technology, the Clawdite bypassed Delrian's automated defenses and escaped off-world with Tambor.<ref name="shadowfeed" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Not surprisingly, this story has yet to be reported in the government-dominated mainstream Republic media.|CIS Shadowfeed report, referring to Wat Tambor's rescue|<ref name="shadowfeed" />}}
Tambor was taken to his private estate in [[Denus]], [[Foundry/Legends|Foundry]], to recuperate in a [[hyperbaric recharge globe]], where he remained for several [[Standard day/Legends|days]]. Via the [[Shadowfeed/Legends|CIS Shadowfeed]], the Separatists lauded the daring of Tambor's staff, who had given their lives for the Separatist cause. The shadowfeed used the rescue as a morale-booster for Confederate worlds, highlighting the boldness of the CIS and the inadequacies of the Republic. Although the involvement of a Clawdite in the mission was known, Nuri's identity was kept secret. The Republic attempted to keep the story from the public, stopping the mainstream media from reporting it.<ref name="shadowfeed" />

Tambor's rescue allowed Palpatine to plot in safety once more; with the Techno Union back to full activity, the war was evenly poised and no end was in sight.<ref name="nec" /> As the conflict progressed, Tambor became extremely reclusive, spending more and more [[Time/Legends|time]] in his [[Mazariyan|fortress]] on [[Xagobah/Legends|Xagobah]]. Nuri, pivotal in the rescue mission, remained in the Techno Union's employ as a guard of the fortress.<ref name="cswe">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|''The New Essential Chronology'']]&mdash;a book published by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic's]] [[Historical Council]] under the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]&mdash;was published in [[36 ABY]] and mentioned the mission.<ref name="nec" />

==Behind the scenes==
The mission to Delrian was first mentioned in the [[in-universe]] news article ''[[CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 14:4:12 Edition]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and published by [[Paizo Publishing]] in [[Star Wars Insider 67|''Star Wars Insider'' 67]]<ref name="shadowfeed" /> on [[April 15]], [[2003]].<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=community/news/2003/03/news20030317.html|text=Celebrate <i>Jedi</i>'s 20th in ''Insider'' #67}}</ref> The mission is a followup to the events of the<ref name="shadowfeed" /> [[2002]]<ref name="Metacritic">{{WebCite|url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/game-boy-advance/star-wars-the-new-droid-army|text=Star Wars: The New Droid Army|work=[https://www.metacritic.com Metacritic]|archivedate=20190527071657}}</ref> video game ''[[Star Wars: The New Droid Army]]''.<ref name="shadowfeed" /> However, the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Heroes on Both Sides]], released in [[2010]],<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode310.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref> established that the Republic capital of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] had not been attacked during the Clone Wars until the events of that episode.<ref name="Heroes">{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref> As "Heroes on Both Sides" is set at the start of the year 20 BBY,<ref name="TCW-Date">{{TCWdates|310}}</ref> both ''The New Droid Army'' and the mission to Delrian had to occur later in the timeline, after the episode.<ref name="Date" />
